# Copilot Instructions
- **Project Layout** root `src/` currently exposes init/logging scaffolding while the playable raycaster lives under `raycaster/`; expect future integration to reuse these foundations.
- **Sandbox Binary** `raycaster/Makefile` builds `sandbox` with `make -C raycaster` (or `make -C raycaster run` to rebuild, execute, then clean object files).
- **Main Target** top-level `Makefile` links `cub3d` against `libft` and system MiniLibX (`-lmlx -lXext -lX11`); `make run` performs a full rebuild (`re`) before launching.
- **Libft Dependency** `make` at the root automatically invokes `make` inside `libft/`; keep its headers in sync with `include/libft.h` when adding helpers.
- **Logging Levels** toggle with `make log0`, `make log2`, etc.; these append `-DLOGGING_LEVEL=n` to `CFLAGS` and rebuild from scratch.
- **Core Data** `include/structs.h` defines `t_data` and `t_map_data` for the final game, mirroring expected `.cub` assets (textures + RGB floor/ceiling).
- **Raycaster Types** `raycaster/include/types.h` expands this into `t_game`, `t_player`, `t_ray`, and `t_keys`; keep additions consistent across the header to avoid mismatched struct layouts.
- **Startup Flow** `raycaster/main.c` seeds `t_game`, calls `init_player`, loads `test_map`, then `init_mlx` and `setup_hooks`; new features should slot into this sequence.
- **Event Handling** `hooks.c` relies on `<X11/keysym.h>` codes; update both press and release handlers when introducing new controls to keep `t_keys` in sync.
- **Frame Loop** `render_loop` in `render.c` is the central heartbeat: update delta time via `get_time`, clear the frame, move/rotate (`new_pos`), cast rays, draw minimap, then blit with `mlx_put_image_to_window`.
- **Movement Rules** `new_pos` scales movement (`speed=5`) and rotation (`rot_speed=3`) by delta time; collision uses `check_wall`, which treats out-of-bounds or `'1'` tiles as solid walls.
- **Map Encoding** The sandbox expects `char **map` rows with `'0'` open, `'1'` wall, and a single orientation character (`N/E/S/W`) for spawn; keep maps rectangular or guard DDA against ragged edges.
- **Ray Casting** `perform_dda` walks the grid until it hits `'1'`; ensure maps are enclosed to prevent OOB reads, and add bounds checks before touching `game->map[ray->map.y][ray->map.x]` when expanding.
- **Ray Init Edge Cases** `init_ray` divides by `ray->dir.x`/`y`; clamp or short-circuit zero-direction components when tweaking FOV or camera plane to avoid infinities.
- **Column Drawing** `draw_column` uses 2D screen coordinates; adjust colors/texturing here, but keep `put_pixel` as the write path because it respects image pitch and endianness.
- **Minimap Rendering** `minimap.c` draws tiles with nested loops using `TILE_SIZE` (20); reuse `get_map_dimensions` if you need bounds before iterating.
- **Player Marker** `draw_player_on_minimap` paints a solid tile at the player grid cell—switch to a smaller overlay if precision aiming is needed, but preserve the per-pixel loops.
- **Timing Utility** `utils.c:get_time` wraps `gettimeofday`; reuse it for animations or cooldowns so everything remains in the same time domain.
- **Cleanup Path** `cleanup.c:cleanup_game` tears down MLX objects and display; extend this when you allocate textures or dynamic maps, but never free the static `test_map` array.
- **Assets Reference** `assets/maps/basic.cub` shows the intended `.cub` layout (texture identifiers + RGB + map); align future parsers with this schema so the sandbox evolves smoothly into the final binary.
- **Header Discipline** Include local headers from `raycaster/include/` using the same relative paths as existing files (for example `"./include/render.h"`) to guarantee consistent prototypes; update headers first when adding new functions.
- **Coding Style** The project follows 42-style prototypes and minimal inline comments; prefer short, descriptive helper names over heavy documentation, adding a comment only when logic is non-obvious.
- **Platform Assumptions** Everything targets Linux MiniLibX; ensure `$DISPLAY` is exported when running under a container and link with `-lm` when you introduce math-heavy code.
